expected: AED price bands distinguished from observed prices
Source, portion, branch and channel context

answer.headline: I can't recommend price bands yet: retrieved UAE menu evidence is thin and brand-agnostic. Here is what it does show, plus the specific pricing data needed.

sections.title: What the retrieved evidence actually shows on price

items.text: Two Papa Johns UAE deal prices are observed: a single-person bundle (small 8-inch pizza, potato wedges, canned drink) and a two-person bundle (medium pizza, two starters, two canned drinks), with the store directory stating branches share the same UAE menu and prices.

Papa Johns UAE says its branches offer delivery and takeaway on a shared menu/pricing structure, and lists branches in both cities (Deira/Al Muraqqabat, Port Saeed, Al Barsha, Marina in Dubai; Al Zahiyah, Al Khalidiya, Al Manhal in Abu Dhabi).

Allo Beirut is the closest retrieved comparable for our sandwich side: its listings include shawarma, grills and sandwiches, with branches on Hessa Street and JBR in Dubai and Al Najda and Khalifa City in Abu Dhabi, and an advertised late-night delivery window in Dubai.

These are bundle prices, not standalone item prices, and the sources do not specify tax treatment, delivery fees, or branch-level availability. Bundle pricing does not let me derive a city-level price band for a meaty pizza or a kebab sandwich.

Both are public branch and website listings; the sources state that presence does not establish sales, market share or footfall. No competitor prices were found for kebab sandwiches or shawarma in either city.

sections.title: Why I am not stating bands (and what a provisional approach would be)

items.text: Stating a Dubai-versus-Abu-Dhabi price band now would require inventing competitor prices, rent or demand assumptions the evidence does not support, so I will not do it.

Provisional method instead: price our meaty pizza relative to the observed small-pizza bundle tier and our kebab sandwich relative to observed fast-casual sandwich competition, then hold a single UAE-wide list menu (as the UAE-wide shared pricing structure suggests) with city-specific delivery bundles rather than two city price lists.

Test rather than set: run one price point for 6-8 weeks in a Dubai site and one in an Abu Dhabi site, comparing mix and contribution, before committing to city bands. Two bundle observations cannot reveal price elasticity or what customers will pay.
To set a floor, cost our own recipe: food cost per pizza and per sandwich, packaging, and delivery commission. Break-even depends on those inputs, which are not set in the profile.

assumptions: Business profile: Jordanian restaurant serving meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches, targeting Dubai and Abu Dhabi; startup budget, rent budget, branch format, positioning and opening date are unset.
Bundles observed are treated as competitor reference points only, not as recommended price points.
next_steps: Pull our own recipe costing for the flagship meaty pizza and kebab sandwich: food cost, packaging, and expected delivery share.

Capture current menu prices for pizza and sandwich/shawarma operators in Dubai (Marina, Al Barsha, Deira) and Abu Dhabi (Al Zahiyah, Al Khalidiya, Khalifa City) from their own sites and delivery apps, recording date, branch, portion and channel.
Separate dine-in/takeaway list prices from delivery-app prices and note fees and tax treatment so comparisons are like-for-like.
questions: What are your current menu prices in Jordan, and the food cost and packaging cost per meaty pizza and per kebab sandwich?
What average order value, delivery share, delivery commission rate, and monthly fixed costs (rent, salaries, utilities) do you expect per branch in Dubai and Abu Dhabi?

rendered_answer:
I can't recommend price bands yet: retrieved UAE menu evidence is thin and brand-agnostic. Here is what it does show, plus the specific pricing data needed.

**What the retrieved evidence actually shows on price**

- **Fact:** Two Papa Johns UAE deal prices are observed: a single-person bundle \(small 8-inch pizza, potato wedges, canned drink\) and a two-person bundle \(medium pizza, two starters, two canned drinks\), with the store directory stating branches share the same UAE menu and prices. [1](<https://www.papajohns.ae/menu>) [2](<https://www.papajohns.ae/stores>)
- **Fact:** Papa Johns UAE says its branches offer delivery and takeaway on a shared menu/pricing structure, and lists branches in both cities \(Deira/Al Muraqqabat, Port Saeed, Al Barsha, Marina in Dubai; Al Zahiyah, Al Khalidiya, Al Manhal in Abu Dhabi\). [2](<https://www.papajohns.ae/stores>)
- **Fact:** Allo Beirut is the closest retrieved comparable for our sandwich side: its listings include shawarma, grills and sandwiches, with branches on Hessa Street and JBR in Dubai and Al Najda and Khalifa City in Abu Dhabi, and an advertised late-night delivery window in Dubai. [3](<https://www.allobeirutstreetfood.com/locations>)
- **Inference:** These are bundle prices, not standalone item prices, and the sources do not specify tax treatment, delivery fees, or branch-level availability. Bundle pricing does not let me derive a city-level price band for a meaty pizza or a kebab sandwich. [1](<https://www.papajohns.ae/menu>)
- **Inference:** Both are public branch and website listings; the sources state that presence does not establish sales, market share or footfall. No competitor prices were found for kebab sandwiches or shawarma in either city. [2](<https://www.papajohns.ae/stores>)

**Why I am not stating bands \(and what a provisional approach would be\)**

- **Inference:** Stating a Dubai-versus-Abu-Dhabi price band now would require inventing competitor prices, rent or demand assumptions the evidence does not support, so I will not do it.
- **Proposal:** Provisional method instead: price our meaty pizza relative to the observed small-pizza bundle tier and our kebab sandwich relative to observed fast-casual sandwich competition, then hold a single UAE-wide list menu \(as the UAE-wide shared pricing structure suggests\) with city-specific delivery bundles rather than two city price lists. [1](<https://www.papajohns.ae/menu>) [2](<https://www.papajohns.ae/stores>)
- **Proposal:** Test rather than set: run one price point for 6-8 weeks in a Dubai site and one in an Abu Dhabi site, comparing mix and contribution, before committing to city bands. Two bundle observations cannot reveal price elasticity or what customers will pay.
- **Assumption:** To set a floor, cost our own recipe: food cost per pizza and per sandwich, packaging, and delivery commission. Break-even depends on those inputs, which are not set in the profile.

**Assumptions and limitations**

- Business profile: Jordanian restaurant serving meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches, targeting Dubai and Abu Dhabi; startup budget, rent budget, branch format, positioning and opening date are unset.
- Bundles observed are treated as competitor reference points only, not as recommended price points.

**Next steps**

- Pull our own recipe costing for the flagship meaty pizza and kebab sandwich: food cost, packaging, and expected delivery share.
- Capture current menu prices for pizza and sandwich/shawarma operators in Dubai \(Marina, Al Barsha, Deira\) and Abu Dhabi \(Al Zahiyah, Al Khalidiya, Khalifa City\) from their own sites and delivery apps, recording date, branch, portion and channel.
- Separate dine-in/takeaway list prices from delivery-app prices and note fees and tax treatment so comparisons are like-for-like.

**Questions**

- What are your current menu prices in Jordan, and the food cost and packaging cost per meaty pizza and per kebab sandwich?
- What average order value, delivery share, delivery commission rate, and monthly fixed costs \(rent, salaries, utilities\) do you expect per branch in Dubai and Abu Dhabi?
